# Build the greet CLI with version information stamped in.
#
#   make build       build for this machine into ./bin
#   make release     cross-compile for Linux, macOS and Windows into ./dist
#   make test        run the tests

PKG      := github.com/Priyadharshan0903/gopath-academy/projects/greet
VERSION  ?= $(shell git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo dev)
COMMIT   ?= $(shell git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo none)
DATE     ?= $(shell date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)

LDFLAGS := -s -w \
	-X $(PKG)/internal/version.Version=$(VERSION) \
	-X $(PKG)/internal/version.Commit=$(COMMIT) \
	-X $(PKG)/internal/version.Date=$(DATE)

PLATFORMS := linux/amd64 linux/arm64 darwin/arm64 windows/amd64

.PHONY: build release test clean

build:
	go build -trimpath -ldflags "$(LDFLAGS)" -o bin/greet ./cmd/greet

release:
	@for p in $(PLATFORMS); do \
		os=$${p%/*}; arch=$${p#*/}; ext=; \
		[ "$$os" = windows ] && ext=.exe; \
		echo "building $$os/$$arch"; \
		CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=$$os GOARCH=$$arch \
			go build -trimpath -ldflags "$(LDFLAGS)" \
			-o dist/greet-$$os-$$arch$$ext ./cmd/greet || exit 1; \
	done

test:
	go test ./...

clean:
	rm -rf bin dist

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS jobs (
    id           bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    queue        text        NOT NULL,
    payload      jsonb       NOT NULL,
    status       text        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued'
                 CHECK (status IN ('queued', 'running', 'done', 'failed')),
    attempts     int         NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    max_attempts int         NOT NULL DEFAULT 5,
    run_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    locked_until timestamptz,
    last_error   text,
    created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Workers look for runnable jobs in one queue, oldest first. A partial
-- index keeps finished jobs out of it.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS jobs_runnable ON jobs (queue, run_at, id)
    WHERE status IN ('queued', 'running');

func TestEnqueueInTransaction(t *testing.T) {
	c := newClient(t)
	ctx := t.Context()

	tx, _ := c.pool.Begin(ctx)
	EnqueueWith(ctx, tx, "q", "rolled back", EnqueueOptions{})
	tx.Rollback(ctx)

	tx, _ = c.pool.Begin(ctx)
	EnqueueWith(ctx, tx, "q", "committed", EnqueueOptions{})
	tx.Commit(ctx)

	counts, _ := c.Counts(ctx, "q")
	if counts["queued"] != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("counts = %v, want exactly the committed job", counts)
	}
}

# GoReleaser configuration for the greet CLI (lesson 14.4).
#
# Try it without publishing anything:
#
#   cd projects/greet
#   goreleaser check
#   goreleaser release --snapshot --clean
#
# Artifacts land in ./dist. In a repository of its own, you would push a
# tag (git tag v1.2.0 && git push --tags) and run `goreleaser release`
# in CI to publish a GitHub release.
version: 2

project_name: greet

before:
  hooks:
    - go test ./...

builds:
  - id: greet
    main: ./cmd/greet
    binary: greet
    env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0 # static binaries: no C toolchain or libc needed
    goos: [linux, darwin, windows]
    goarch: [amd64, arm64]
    flags:
      - -trimpath # no local file paths in the binary
    ldflags:
      - -s -w
      - -X github.com/Priyadharshan0903/gopath-academy/projects/greet/internal/version.Version={{ .Version }}
      - -X github.com/Priyadharshan0903/gopath-academy/projects/greet/internal/version.Commit={{ .ShortCommit }}
      - -X github.com/Priyadharshan0903/gopath-academy/projects/greet/internal/version.Date={{ .CommitDate }}
    # Use the commit time, not the build time, so rebuilding the same
    # commit produces identical archives.
    mod_timestamp: "{{ .CommitTimestamp }}"

archives:
  - formats: [tar.gz]
    format_overrides:
      - goos: windows
        formats: [zip]
    name_template: "{{ .ProjectName }}_{{ .Version }}_{{ .Os }}_{{ .Arch }}"
    files:
      - README.md

checksum:
  name_template: checksums.txt

snapshot:
  version_template: "{{ incpatch .Version }}-snapshot+{{ .ShortCommit }}"

changelog:
  sort: asc
  filters:
    exclude: ["^docs:", "^test:"]

example-409.code:
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
#
# Container image for the shortener (lesson 15.1). From this directory:
#
#   go mod tidy                       # once, so go.sum exists
#   docker build -t shortener:dev .
#   docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 shortener:dev

# ---------- build stage: the full Go toolchain ----------
FROM golang:1.27 AS build
WORKDIR /src

# Download dependencies in their own layer: it is rebuilt only when
# go.mod or go.sum change, not on every code change.
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod \
    go mod download

COPY . .
# TARGETOS and TARGETARCH are set by docker buildx for each platform of
# a multi-platform build (--platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64). Go
# cross-compiles, so the build stage never needs emulation.
ARG TARGETOS=linux
ARG TARGETARCH=amd64
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod \
    --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/go-build \
    CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=$TARGETOS GOARCH=$TARGETARCH \
    go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" -o /out/shortener ./cmd/shortener

# ---------- runtime stage: just the binary ----------
# distroless/static has CA certificates, time zone data, /etc/passwd
# with a nonroot user, and nothing else: no shell, no package manager.
FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot
COPY --from=build /out/shortener /shortener
# A numeric user, so Kubernetes can verify runAsNonRoot (lesson 15.2).
USER 65532:65532
EXPOSE 8080 9090
ENTRYPOINT ["/shortener"]

example-410.code:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: shortener
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: shortener
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: shortener
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 0 # never go below the desired number of ready pods
      maxSurge: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: shortener
    spec:
      # Longer than SHUTDOWN_DELAY + SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT, so the kubelet never
      # has to SIGKILL a pod that is still finishing requests.
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 65532
        runAsGroup: 65532
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
        - name: shortener
          image: shortener:dev
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
            - name: admin
              containerPort: 9090
          env:
            - name: BASE_URL
              value: http://shortener.localtest.me
            - name: LOG_LEVEL
              value: info
            # Keep serving, unready, while endpoints are updated (lesson 12.8).
            - name: SHUTDOWN_DELAY
              value: 5s
            - name: SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT
              value: 20s
            # Rate limits must key on the client, not on the ingress pod.
            - name: CLIENT_IP_HEADER
              value: X-Real-Ip
            # About 90% of the memory limit below (lesson 11.3).
            - name: GOMEMLIMIT
              value: 115MiB
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 64Mi
            limits:
              cpu: "1"       # Go 1.25+ sets GOMAXPROCS from this (lesson 11.1)
              memory: 128Mi
          startupProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 2
            failureThreshold: 30
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /readyz
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 5
            failureThreshold: 1
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 10
            failureThreshold: 3
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities:
              drop: ["ALL"]

# A complete local setup (k3s, kind, Docker Desktop): the shortener with
# PostgreSQL and Redis running in the cluster.
#
#   docker build -t shortener:dev projects/shortener
#   (load the image into the cluster, see lesson 15.2)
#   kubectl apply -k projects/shortener/k8s/overlays/local
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: shortener
resources:
  - namespace.yaml
  - ../../base
  - postgres.yaml
  - redis.yaml
secretGenerator:
  # Local development values only. Real clusters get secrets from a
  # secret manager (External Secrets, Sealed Secrets, Vault), never git.
  - name: postgres
    literals:
      - password=local-dev-only
  - name: shortener-db
    literals:
      - database-url=postgres://postgres:local-dev-only@postgres:5432/postgres?sslmode=disable
patches:
  - path: deployment-patch.yaml

callout-0.body: This course is written for **Go 1.27**. Thanks to the compatibility promise, almost everything here also works on older 1.2x versions. When a feature is newer, the lesson says which version introduced it.

callout-1.body: Always remove the old `/usr/local/go` before extracting a new version. Extracting on top of an old install mixes files from two versions and causes confusing errors.

callout-2.body: **A bit of history.** Before Go 1.11, all Go code had to live inside `GOPATH/src`, and older tutorials still describe that layout. With modules (lesson 1.4) your projects can live anywhere on disk. You can ignore advice that tells you to put code in `GOPATH`.

callout-3.body: Use `go run .` (a dot, meaning "the package in this directory") instead of `go run main.go`. As soon as your program has a second file, `go run main.go` fails because it only compiles the files you list.

callout-4.body: You will find a popular repository called "golang-standards/project-layout". Despite the name, it is **not** an official standard and is not maintained by the Go team. The official guidance is [Organizing a Go module](https://go.dev/doc/modules/layout), and it is much simpler.

callout-5.body: golangci-lint recommends installing a pinned release binary rather than using `go install`, so that everyone gets the same build. Follow the [install guide](https://golangci-lint.run/welcome/install/) for your platform. You can also pin it with the `tool` directive from lesson 1.4.

callout-6.body: One important exception: a `nil` **map** can be read, but writing to it panics. You must create maps with `make` or a literal before adding keys. Lesson 3.5 covers this.

callout-7.body: Always write `s = append(s, x)`. The compiler rejects an `append` whose result is not used, because forgetting to assign it is always a bug.

callout-8.body: You will still see `sort.Slice` and `sort.Strings` in older code. They work, but `slices.Sort` and `slices.SortFunc` are faster and type safe. Prefer them in new code.

callout-9.body: Never call `fmt.Sprintf("%v", x)` on the receiver itself inside `String()`. It calls `String()` again and recurses until the stack overflows. Convert to the underlying type first, as `int(d)` does above.

callout-10.body: The examples in this lesson need **Go 1.27 or newer**. Their files start with `//go:build go1.27`, so older toolchains skip them.

callout-11.body: **What changed in Go 1.27.** The new packages `encoding/json/v2` and `encoding/json/jsontext` are now generally available, and the classic `encoding/json` package is now implemented **on top of v2**. Its behavior is preserved and you do not need to migrate, but **error message text may differ** from older releases. Never match on JSON error strings; check error types instead, as the examples do.

callout-12.body: The examples below need **Go 1.27 or newer**; their file is gated with `//go:build go1.27`.

callout-13.body: `testing/synctest` is available from **Go 1.25**. The examples here are gated with `//go:build go1.25`.

disclosure-0.title: Hint 1: where the starter allocates
disclosure-0.body: Four places: `strings.Fields` allocates a slice for every post; `tag += string(r)` allocates a new string for every character; `strings.ToLower` allocates even when the tag is already lowercase; and the sort comparator calls `fmt.Sprintf` twice on every comparison.

disclosure-1.title: Hint 2: substrings are free
disclosure-1.body: A substring like `post[i+1:j]` shares memory with `post` and does not allocate. Using it as a map key does not allocate either. Scan the bytes of each post directly instead of splitting it into words.

disclosure-3.title: Check your answers
disclosure-3.body:
1. 16 (string) + 8 + 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 41 bytes.
2. 8 bytes.
3. 41 rounded up to a multiple of 8 is **48**. So 48 is not just a target; it is the minimum.

disclosure-4.title: Hint: where do the 64 bytes come from?
disclosure-4.body: Use `unsafe.Offsetof` on each field of the starter, or reason it through: `Active` (1 byte) is followed by 7 bytes of padding so `ID` starts at offset 8; `Kind` by 7 more before `Score`; `Retries` by 6 before `Name`. That is 20 bytes of padding inside, plus 3 at the end.

disclosure-5.title: Hint 1: the routes
disclosure-5.body: Four patterns with methods: `"GET /notes"`, `"POST /notes"`, `"GET /notes/{id}"` and `"DELETE /notes/{id}"`. With methods in the patterns, ServeMux produces the 405 responses by itself (lesson 12.1).

disclosure-6.title: Hint 2: an empty list
disclosure-6.body: `json.Marshal` turns a nil slice into `null`, not `[]`. `Store.List` returns a non-nil empty slice, so encoding it directly gives `[]`. Keep it that way.

disclosure-7.title: Hint 3: keep handlers short
disclosure-7.body: Write two small helpers: `writeJSON(w, status, v)`, which sets `Content-Type` before `WriteHeader`, and `parseID(w, r)`, which writes the 400 itself and returns `(id, ok)`.

disclosure-8.title: Hint 1: the data
disclosure-8.body: Two maps behind one `sync.Mutex`: `entries` (value and expiry time) and `inflight` (loads in progress). A load in progress is a small struct with a `done` channel and fields for the result.

disclosure-9.title: Hint 2: the lock
disclosure-9.body: Rule 5 means you must **not** hold the mutex while calling the loader. Lock, look in both maps, register a new in-flight call if needed, unlock, load, then lock again to store the result and remove the in-flight entry.

disclosure-10.title: Hint 3: waking the waiters
disclosure-10.body: Closing a channel wakes every goroutine blocked on receiving from it (lesson 6.2). Write the result into the call struct **before** closing `done`; the close makes the writes visible to the waiters (lesson 6.7). Waiters should also give up if their own context ends.

disclosure-11.title: Hint 4: the clock
disclosure-11.body: Never call `time.Now()` directly; use the `now` function you were given, so the test's fake clock controls expiry.

disclosure-12.title: Hint 1: two levels of flags
disclosure-12.body: Parse the global flags with one `FlagSet`; `fs.Args()` then starts with the command name. Give `list` its own `FlagSet` for `-all`. Use `flag.ContinueOnError` everywhere so `Run` decides the exit code (lesson 14.1).

disclosure-13.title: Hint 2: one place for exit codes
disclosure-13.body: Write an inner `run` that returns an `error`, wrap usage problems with a sentinel such as `errUsage`, and convert to an exit code once in `Run` with `errors.Is`. Do not forget `flag.ErrHelp`: `-h` is success.

disclosure-14.title: Hint 3: precedence
disclosure-14.body: The `-file` flag wins over `$TODO_FILE`, which wins over `todo.json`. Since the flag's default is `""`, an empty value means "not given" here, so `fs.Visit` is not needed (lesson 14.2).

disclosure-15.title: Hint 1: two things to wait for
disclosure-15.body: Run `srv.Serve(ln)` in a goroutine that sends its result on a buffered channel. Then `select` on that channel (the server failed on its own) and on `ctx.Done()` (time to shut down).

disclosure-16.title: Hint 2: the delay
disclosure-16.body: Use a `select` on a timer and the serve channel, not `time.Sleep`, so a server that dies during the delay is reported at once.

disclosure-17.title: Hint 3: the return value
disclosure-17.body: After `Shutdown`, `Serve` returns `http.ErrServerClosed`: that is success, not an error. Receive it from the channel so the goroutine does not leak, and return what `Shutdown` returned.

m01/greeting.title: 1.3 Your first program, line by line
m01/greeting.body: Implement `Greeting(name string) string` so it returns `Hello, <name>!`. Ignore leading and trailing spaces, and use `Gopher` when the name is empty. Look at [`strings.TrimSpace`](https://pkg.go.dev/strings#TrimSpace).

m01/tempconv.title: 1.5 Packages, visibility and project layout
m01/tempconv.body: Implement `CToF`, `FToC` and `IsPhysical` in the `tempconv` package. The tests are in an **external** test package (`tempconv_test`), so they can only call exported names. Notice how that forces you to think about the package from a caller's point of view.

m01/cli.title: 1.8 Checkpoint project: the greet CLI
m01/cli.body: Implement `Parse(args []string) (Config, error)` and `Render(cfg Config) string`. Use a `flag.FlagSet` with `flag.ContinueOnError`, validate that `-times` is at least 1, and return `ErrInvalidTimes` when it is not. The starter file contains detailed requirements.

m02/palindrome.title: 2.4 Strings, bytes, runes and UTF-8
m02/palindrome.body: Implement `Reverse` so it works for any UTF-8 text, and `IsPalindrome`, which ignores case and anything that is not a letter or digit. The tests include accented letters and Chinese characters, so byte-based solutions will fail.

m02/stats.title: 2.6 Functions: multiple returns, variadics and closures
m02/stats.body: Implement `Sum` (variadic), `MinMax` (multiple results with an `ok` flag) and `RunningAverage`, which returns a closure that remembers every value it has seen. The tests check that two running averages do not share state.

m02/ptr.title: 2.8 Pointers without fear
m02/ptr.body: Implement `Swap`, `Clamp` (which must not panic on a nil pointer), `ValueOr` and `IntPtr`. The tests check nil handling and that `IntPtr` gives a fresh pointer on every call.

m03/ints.title: 3.2 Slices: length, capacity and the backing array
m03/ints.body: Implement `Chunk`, `RemoveAt` and `Dedupe`. The tests check that results never share memory with their inputs, so a solution that works on a quick glance but aliases the backing array will fail. Think about capacity.

m03/inventory.title: 3.5 Maps: usage, iteration order, concurrency warning
m03/inventory.body: Implement `Add`, `Remove`, `Merge` and `LowStock`. `Remove` must not create entries for missing items and must delete items that reach zero. `Merge` must return a new map without modifying its inputs, and handle `nil` arguments. `LowStock` must return a sorted result.

m03/seq.title: 3.8 Iterators and range-over-func
m03/seq.body: Implement `Range`, `Map` and `Take`. The tests run your functions on an **infinite** iterator and count how many values were pulled, so `Take` must stop pulling as soon as it has enough, and every function must respect early `break`.

m04/kv.title: 4.2 Interfaces: implicit satisfaction and small interfaces
m04/kv.body: Implement `MemStore`, then two **decorators**: `Prefixed`, which namespaces keys, and `Counting`, which records hits, misses and sets. Both wrap any `Store`, so the last test stacks them on top of each other. Decide which receivers need to be pointers.

m04/set.title: 4.6 Generics: type parameters and constraints
m04/set.body: Build a generic `Set[T comparable]` with `New`, `Add`, `Has`, `Len` and `Union`, plus a function `Sorted[T cmp.Ordered]`. Think about why `Sorted` is a function rather than a method: the set only requires `comparable`, but sorting needs ordering. The tests use strings, ints and a struct type.

m05/config.title: 5.2 Wrapping with %w, errors.Is and errors.As
m05/config.body: Build a small config parser. `ParseLine` returns errors wrapping `ErrSyntax`. `Load` returns a `*ParseError` with the line number, whose `Unwrap` method exposes the cause, so callers can use both `errors.As` (to get the line) and `errors.Is` (to check `ErrSyntax` or `ErrDuplicateKey`).

m05/form.title: 5.4 errors.Join and multi-errors
m05/form.body: Implement `FieldError`, a `Validate` function that reports every problem in a signup form with `errors.Join`, and a `Fields` helper that lists the failed fields by unwrapping the joined error. The tests check both the exact message and that `errors.Is` finds every sentinel.

m06/pipeline.title: 6.2 Channels: unbuffered, buffered, direction
m06/pipeline.body: Implement `Generate`, `Square` and `Merge`. Each function creates and closes its own output channel, and every goroutine must exit when its input is drained. The last test counts goroutines before and after running 50 pipelines, so a missing `close` or a stuck goroutine will fail it. Run with `go test -race`.

m06/parallel.title: 6.4 sync.WaitGroup, WaitGroup.Go, Mutex, RWMutex and Once
m06/parallel.body: Implement `Sum`, which splits a slice across worker goroutines, and `Tally`, a concurrency-safe counter whose zero value works and whose `Snapshot` returns a copy. Run the tests with `go test -race`; the race detector must stay silent.

m07/poll.title: 7.1 context.Context: cancellation, deadlines, values
m07/poll.body: Implement `WaitFor`, which polls a condition until it is true or the context ends, and `Retry`, which retries with exponential backoff but stops waiting the moment the context is cancelled. The tests measure timing, so a solution that sleeps without watching `ctx.Done()` will fail.

m07/pmap.title: 7.2 Worker pools
m07/pmap.body: Write a generic `Map` that runs a function over a slice with a fixed number of workers, returns results **in input order**, cancels the remaining work on the first error, and never leaks goroutines. The tests check ordering, the concurrency limit, cancellation and leaks.

m08/grep.title: 8.1 io: composing readers and writers
m08/grep.body: Build a small `Grep` on top of `bufio.Scanner` and `bufio.Writer`, with line numbers and inverted matching, and a `CountingReader` wrapper. The tests use `testing/iotest` to feed your code half-sized reads and failing readers, and to check that your reader follows the `io.Reader` contract.

m08/apiclient.title: 8.7 net/http client done right
m08/apiclient.body: Write a small API client with `GetUser` and `CreateUser`. It must send the right headers, respect the context, map `404` to `ErrNotFound` and other failures to an `*APIError` that carries the server's error message, and decode JSON responses. The tests run against an `httptest` server, including a slow endpoint that must time out.

m09/fizzhttp.title: 9.5 httptest
m09/fizzhttp.body: Implement an HTTP handler for `GET /fizzbuzz?n=N` that validates input, sets headers, returns JSON and rejects other methods with `405` and an `Allow` header. The tests use both `NewRecorder` and `NewServer`.

m09/rle.title: 9.6 Fuzzing
m09/rle.body: Implement a run-length `Encode` and `Decode`. The tests include two fuzz targets: a round-trip property and a "never panic, and anything accepted re-encodes consistently" property. After the unit tests pass, run `go test -fuzz=FuzzRoundTrip -fuzztime=20s ./m09/rle` and see whether the fuzzer can break your code (runs longer than 255 are a common trap).

m10/hashtags.title: 10.7 Exercise: optimize under an allocation budget
m10/hashtags.body: `TopTags` finds the most common hashtags in a list of posts. Make `TestAllocationBudget` pass (at most 400 allocations for 1000 posts) while keeping `TestTopTags` and `TestTiesAreAlphabetical` green. Use the workflow from this module: run the benchmark, read a memory profile, fix the biggest source, measure again.

m11/layout.title: 11.7 Exercise: shrink a struct
m11/layout.body: `Event` is 64 bytes on a 64-bit platform. Reorder its fields so that `unsafe.Sizeof(Event{})` is 48 bytes. You may not add, remove, rename or change the type of any field; `TestFieldsUnchanged` checks that with reflection.

m12/notes.title: 12.7 Exercise: a notes JSON API
m12/notes.body: Implement `NewHandler` in `starter.go`. The tests check every row of the specification, including headers and the 405 responses.

m13/readthrough.title: 13.6 Exercise: a read-through cache
m13/readthrough.body: Implement `Cache.Get` so that it follows the five rules in the comment on `Cache`: hits skip the loader, values expire after the TTL, errors are not cached, concurrent misses for one key share a single load, and a slow load never blocks other keys.

m14/todo.title: 14.5 Exercise: a to-do CLI
m14/todo.body: Implement `Run` in `starter.go`: a to-do list with the subcommands `add`, `list` (with `-all`) and `done`, a global `-file` flag that falls back to `$TODO_FILE` and then `todo.json`, and the exit codes 0, 1 and 2 as specified. `load` and `save` in `store.go` handle the JSON file for you.

m15/drain.title: 15.6 Exercise: drain gracefully
m15/drain.body: Implement `Serve` in `starter.go`: serve until the context is cancelled, then mark the service not ready, keep serving for `opts.Delay`, and shut down with `srv.Shutdown`, giving in-flight requests up to `opts.Timeout`.

examples/README.md.content:
# Examples

Every code sample on the website is embedded from a file in this folder, and every file here is tested.

```bash
go test ./examples/...          # all examples
go test -v ./examples/m01/...   # module 1, verbose
go run ./examples/m01/hello     # run a single program
```

Folders are named `mNN/<topic>`, where `NN` is the module number.

examples/thirdparty/README.md.content:
# Third party examples

Examples that use packages outside the standard library live in this
separate module, so the main course module stays dependency-free.

```bash
cd examples/thirdparty
go mod tidy      # downloads dependencies and writes go.sum the first time
go test ./...
```

CI runs the same commands. Dependencies are pinned in `go.mod`.

## Databases (Module 13)

Tests that need PostgreSQL or Redis are **skipped** unless these
variables are set. Each database test creates its own schema and drops
it afterwards, so any scratch database works.

```bash
docker run -d --name gopath-pg -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pg -p 5432:5432 postgres:16
docker run -d --name gopath-redis -p 6379:6379 redis:7

export TEST_DATABASE_URL='postgres://postgres:pg@localhost:5432/postgres?sslmode=disable'
export TEST_REDIS_ADDR='localhost:6379'
go test ./db/... ./cache/...
```

| Package | Lesson |
|---|---|
| `observability` | 12.5 Prometheus metrics and OpenTelemetry tracing |
| `db/sqlbasics` | 13.1 `database/sql`, pooling, SQL injection |
| `db/pgxdemo` | 13.2 pgx: structs, errors, batch and COPY |
| `db/txdemo` | 13.4 transactions, lost updates, deadlocks, cancellation |
| `cache/rediscache` | 13.5 cache-aside with Redis and request coalescing |

Each folder is one exercise. Edit `starter.go` until the tests pass.

```bash
cd exercises
go test ./m01/greeting/      # one exercise
go test ./m01/...            # all exercises in module 1
```

The tests fail until your code is correct. That is expected.

```bash
go test -tags solution ./m01/greeting/
```

projects/crawler/README.md.content:
# crawler

Concurrent web crawler, the project for Part 2 (Modules 6 and 7).

- A coordinator goroutine owns the queue and the seen-set; workers only fetch.
- Bounded concurrency, depth and page limits, a shared rate limiter, and `context` cancellation.
- Tested against a local `httptest` site: no network needed.

```bash
go test -race ./...
go run ./cmd/crawler -url http://localhost:1313/ -depth 2   # crawl the course site while running `make serve`
```

Only crawl sites you own or have permission to crawl.

projects/greet/.goreleaser.yaml.content:
# GoReleaser configuration for the greet CLI (lesson 14.4).
#
# Try it without publishing anything:
#
#   cd projects/greet
#   goreleaser check
#   goreleaser release --snapshot --clean
#
# Artifacts land in ./dist. In a repository of its own, you would push a
# tag (git tag v1.2.0 && git push --tags) and run `goreleaser release`
# in CI to publish a GitHub release.
version: 2

project_name: greet

before:
  hooks:
    - go test ./...

builds:
  - id: greet
    main: ./cmd/greet
    binary: greet
    env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0 # static binaries: no C toolchain or libc needed
    goos: [linux, darwin, windows]
    goarch: [amd64, arm64]
    flags:
      - -trimpath # no local file paths in the binary
    ldflags:
      - -s -w
      - -X github.com/Priyadharshan0903/gopath-academy/projects/greet/internal/version.Version={{ .Version }}
      - -X github.com/Priyadharshan0903/gopath-academy/projects/greet/internal/version.Commit={{ .ShortCommit }}
      - -X github.com/Priyadharshan0903/gopath-academy/projects/greet/internal/version.Date={{ .CommitDate }}
    # Use the commit time, not the build time, so rebuilding the same
    # commit produces identical archives.
    mod_timestamp: "{{ .CommitTimestamp }}"

archives:
  - formats: [tar.gz]
    format_overrides:
      - goos: windows
        formats: [zip]
    name_template: "{{ .ProjectName }}_{{ .Version }}_{{ .Os }}_{{ .Arch }}"
    files:
      - README.md

checksum:
  name_template: checksums.txt

snapshot:
  version_template: "{{ incpatch .Version }}-snapshot+{{ .ShortCommit }}"

changelog:
  sort: asc
  filters:
    exclude: ["^docs:", "^test:"]

projects/greet/Makefile.content:
# Build the greet CLI with version information stamped in.
#
#   make build       build for this machine into ./bin
#   make release     cross-compile for Linux, macOS and Windows into ./dist
#   make test        run the tests

PKG      := github.com/Priyadharshan0903/gopath-academy/projects/greet
VERSION  ?= $(shell git describe --tags --always --dirty 2>/dev/null || echo dev)
COMMIT   ?= $(shell git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo none)
DATE     ?= $(shell date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)

LDFLAGS := -s -w \
	-X $(PKG)/internal/version.Version=$(VERSION) \
	-X $(PKG)/internal/version.Commit=$(COMMIT) \
	-X $(PKG)/internal/version.Date=$(DATE)

PLATFORMS := linux/amd64 linux/arm64 darwin/arm64 windows/amd64

.PHONY: build release test clean

build:
	go build -trimpath -ldflags "$(LDFLAGS)" -o bin/greet ./cmd/greet

release:
	@for p in $(PLATFORMS); do \
		os=$${p%/*}; arch=$${p#*/}; ext=; \
		[ "$$os" = windows ] && ext=.exe; \
		echo "building $$os/$$arch"; \
		CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=$$os GOARCH=$$arch \
			go build -trimpath -ldflags "$(LDFLAGS)" \
			-o dist/greet-$$os-$$arch$$ext ./cmd/greet || exit 1; \
	done

test:
	go test ./...

clean:
	rm -rf bin dist

projects/jobqueue/README.md.content:
# jobqueue

A background job queue stored in PostgreSQL: the Module 13 project.

- **Enqueue** jobs with a JSON payload, a delay and a retry limit, optionally inside your own transaction (`EnqueueWith`), so a job exists only if the work that created it committed.
- **Workers** claim jobs with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, so many workers (in one process or many) never take the same job.
- **Retries** with exponential backoff and jitter; jobs that keep failing end up `failed` with their last error.
- **Crash recovery**: a claimed job is locked for a visibility timeout; if its worker dies, another worker picks it up when the lock expires.
- **Graceful shutdown**: cancelling `Run` stops claiming new jobs and waits for running ones.

Delivery is **at least once**: a job can run twice if a worker dies after doing the work but before recording it. Handlers must be idempotent.

This directory is its own Go module (it depends on pgx).

## Run the tests

The tests need PostgreSQL and are skipped without it:

```bash
docker run -d --name gopath-pg -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pg -p 5432:5432 postgres:16
```

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS jobs (
    id           bigint GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY,
    queue        text        NOT NULL,
    payload      jsonb       NOT NULL,
    status       text        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued'
                 CHECK (status IN ('queued', 'running', 'done', 'failed')),
    attempts     int         NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    max_attempts int         NOT NULL DEFAULT 5,
    run_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    locked_until timestamptz,
    last_error   text,
    created_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
    updated_at   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);

-- Workers look for runnable jobs in one queue, oldest first. A partial
-- index keeps finished jobs out of it.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS jobs_runnable ON jobs (queue, run_at, id)
    WHERE status IN ('queued', 'running');

projects/miniredis/README.md.content:
# miniredis

A small Redis-compatible server: the Module 8 project.

- `internal/resp`: RESP2 protocol reader and writer (with a fuzz test)
- `internal/store`: concurrency-safe keyspace with expiry and a janitor goroutine
- `internal/aof`: append-only file persistence and crash-tolerant replay
- `internal/server`: TCP server, one goroutine per client, graceful shutdown

```bash
go test -race ./...
go run ./cmd/miniredis -addr 127.0.0.1:6380 -aof /tmp/mini.aof
redis-cli -p 6380 set greeting hello
redis-cli -p 6380 get greeting
```

Supported commands: PING, ECHO, GET, SET (with EX), DEL, EXISTS, INCR, EXPIRE, TTL, DBSIZE.

projects/shortener/Dockerfile.content:
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
#
# Container image for the shortener (lesson 15.1). From this directory:
#
#   go mod tidy                       # once, so go.sum exists
#   docker build -t shortener:dev .
#   docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 shortener:dev

# ---------- build stage: the full Go toolchain ----------
FROM golang:1.27 AS build
WORKDIR /src

# Download dependencies in their own layer: it is rebuilt only when
# go.mod or go.sum change, not on every code change.
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod \
    go mod download

COPY . .
# TARGETOS and TARGETARCH are set by docker buildx for each platform of
# a multi-platform build (--platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64). Go
# cross-compiles, so the build stage never needs emulation.
ARG TARGETOS=linux
ARG TARGETARCH=amd64
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod \
    --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/go-build \
    CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=$TARGETOS GOARCH=$TARGETARCH \
    go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" -o /out/shortener ./cmd/shortener

# ---------- runtime stage: just the binary ----------
# distroless/static has CA certificates, time zone data, /etc/passwd
# with a nonroot user, and nothing else: no shell, no package manager.
FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot
COPY --from=build /out/shortener /shortener
# A numeric user, so Kubernetes can verify runAsNonRoot (lesson 15.2).
USER 65532:65532
EXPOSE 8080 9090
ENTRYPOINT ["/shortener"]

projects/shortener/k8s/base/deployment.y.content:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: shortener
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: shortener
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: shortener
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 0 # never go below the desired number of ready pods
      maxSurge: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: shortener
    spec:
      # Longer than SHUTDOWN_DELAY + SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT, so the kubelet never
      # has to SIGKILL a pod that is still finishing requests.
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 65532
        runAsGroup: 65532
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
        - name: shortener
          image: shortener:dev
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
            - name: admin
              containerPort: 9090
          env:
            - name: BASE_URL
              value: http://shortener.localtest.me
            - name: LOG_LEVEL
              value: info
            # Keep serving, unready, while endpoints are updated (lesson 12.8).
            - name: SHUTDOWN_DELAY
              value: 5s
            - name: SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT
              value: 20s
            # Rate limits must key on the client, not on the ingress pod.
            - name: CLIENT_IP_HEADER
              value: X-Real-Ip
            # About 90% of the memory limit below (lesson 11.3).
            - name: GOMEMLIMIT
              value: 115MiB
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 100m
              memory: 64Mi
            limits:
              cpu: "1"       # Go 1.25+ sets GOMAXPROCS from this (lesson 11.1)
              memory: 128Mi
          startupProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 2
            failureThreshold: 30
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /readyz
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 5
            failureThreshold: 1
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 10
            failureThreshold: 3
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities:
              drop: ["ALL"]

# A complete local setup (k3s, kind, Docker Desktop): the shortener with

  - name: shortener-db
    literals:
      - database-url=postgres://postgres:local-dev-only@postgres:5432/postgres?sslmode=disable

projects/shortener/README.md.content:
# shortener

A URL shortener built across several modules of the course.

| Milestone | Module | What is added | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Core | 5 (Errors) | `internal/link`: domain type, sentinel errors, validation, `Service`, in-memory `Store` | done |
| 2. HTTP API | 12 (HTTP services) | `internal/httpapi`, `internal/config`, `cmd/shortener`: JSON API, redirects, middleware, metrics, graceful shutdown | done |
| 3. Postgres | 13 (Working with data) | `internal/postgres` (pgx store, embedded migrations), `internal/cache` (Redis), `internal/link/linktest` (store conformance suite) | done |
| 4. Kubernetes | 15 (Cloud native) | `Dockerfile`, `k8s/` (Kustomize base and local overlay), `DELETE` endpoint for the ShortLink operator | done |

This directory is its own Go module, because it uses third party packages (pgx, go-redis, the Prometheus client, `golang.org/x/time/rate` and `golang.org/x/sync`). The rest of the course has no dependencies.

## Layout

```text
cmd/shortener/      main: wiring, servers, graceful shutdown
internal/link/      the domain: Link, Service, Store, errors (milestone 1)
internal/link/linktest/  conformance tests every Store must pass
internal/httpapi/   routes, JSON, error mapping, middleware, metrics, rate limiting
internal/config/    configuration from environment variables
internal/postgres/  PostgreSQL Store and migrations
internal/cache/     Redis cache in front of any Store
internal/pgtest/    test helper: a fresh schema per test
```

## Run it

```bash
cd projects/shortener
go mod tidy          # first time only: downloads dependencies
go test ./...
LOG_FORMAT=text go run ./cmd/shortener
```

Without `DATABASE_URL`, links are kept in memory. With PostgreSQL and Redis:

```bash
docker run -d --name gopath-pg -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=pg -p 5432:5432 postgres:16
docker run -d --name gopath-redis -p 6379:6379 redis:7
export DATABASE_URL='postgres://postgres:pg@localhost:5432/postgres?sslmode=disable'
REDIS_ADDR=localhost:6379 LOG_FORMAT=text go run ./cmd/shortener
```

Database tests are skipped unless `TEST_DATABASE_URL` (and, for the cache, `TEST_REDIS_ADDR`) are set:

```bash
export TEST_DATABASE_URL="$DATABASE_URL" TEST_REDIS_ADDR=localhost:6379
go test -race ./...
```

With the service running, in another terminal:

```bash
curl -i -X POST localhost:8080/api/links -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"url": "https://go.dev/doc", "code": "godoc"}'
curl -i localhost:8080/godoc            # 302 to https://go.dev/doc
curl -s localhost:9090/metrics | grep shortener_
```

## Kubernetes

See lesson 15.7. In short: build the image, load it into a local cluster, then `kubectl apply -k k8s/overlays/local`. The ShortLink operator in `projects/shortlink-operator` manages links declaratively.

## API

| Method and path | Success | Errors |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /api/links` with `{"url": "...", "code": "optional"}` | 201, link JSON, `Location` header | 400 bad JSON, 409 code taken, 415 wrong content type, 422 invalid URL or code, 429 rate limited |
| `GET /api/links/{code}` | 200, link JSON | 404, 422, 429 |
| `DELETE /api/links/{code}` | 204 | 404, 422, 429 |
| `GET /{code}` | 302 redirect to the target | 404, 422, 429 |
| `GET /healthz` | 200 while the process runs (liveness) | |
| `GET /readyz` | 200 while accepting traffic (readiness) | 503 before start-up completes and during shutdown |

Errors are `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457) and include the request ID. Server errors are logged in full but never shown to clients.

The admin port serves `GET /metrics` (Prometheus) and `/debug/pprof/`. Never expose it publicly.

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `ADDR` | `:8080` | API listen address |
| `ADMIN_ADDR` | `:9090` | metrics and pprof listen address |
| `BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8080` | public URL, used in `short_url` |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `info` | `debug`, `info`, `warn` or `error` |
| `LOG_FORMAT` | `json` | `json` or `text` |
| `RATE_LIMIT` | `5` | requests per second per client |
| `RATE_BURST` | `10` | burst size per client |
| `CLIENT_IP_HEADER` | (none) | header with the client IP, such as `X-Real-IP`; only set this behind a proxy that always sets it |
| `SHUTDOWN_DELAY` | `0s` | time to keep serving while reporting not ready, before shutting down (use about 5s in Kubernetes) |
| `SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT` | `10s` | time allowed for in-flight requests during shutdown |
| `DATABASE_URL` or `DATABASE_URL_FILE` | (none: in memory) | PostgreSQL connection URL, or a file containing it |
| `MIGRATE` | `true` | apply migrations at start-up |
| `REDIS_ADDR` | (none: no cache) | Redis address, such as `localhost:6379` |
| `CACHE_TTL` | `1h` | how long links stay in the cache |

projects/shortlink-operator/config/manag.content:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: shortlink-operator
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: shortlink-operator
spec:
  replicas: 2 # one leader works, the other waits to take over
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: shortlink-operator
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: shortlink-operator
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: shortlink-operator
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 10
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
        - name: manager
          image: shortlink-operator:dev
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          args:
            - --leader-elect
            - --shortener-url=http://shortener.shortener.svc.cluster.local
          ports:
            - name: metrics
              containerPort: 8080
            - name: probes
              containerPort: 8081
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: probes
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /readyz
              port: probes
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 50m
              memory: 64Mi
            limits:
              memory: 128Mi
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities:
              drop: ["ALL"]

projects/shortlink-operator/Dockerfile.content:
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# Container image for the ShortLink operator (lesson 15.4).
#   go mod tidy && docker build -t shortlink-operator:dev .
FROM golang:1.27 AS build
WORKDIR /src
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod go mod download
COPY . .
ARG TARGETOS=linux
ARG TARGETARCH=amd64
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod \
    --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/go-build \
    CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=$TARGETOS GOARCH=$TARGETARCH \
    go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" -o /out/manager ./cmd/manager

FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot
COPY --from=build /out/manager /manager
# A numeric user, so Kubernetes can verify runAsNonRoot (lesson 15.2).
USER 65532:65532
ENTRYPOINT ["/manager"]

projects/shortlink-operator/README.md.content:
# shortlink-operator

A Kubernetes operator for the course's URL shortener (lessons 15.4 and 15.5). A `ShortLink` custom resource declares a short link; the operator creates it through the shortener's HTTP API, keeps it pointing at `spec.url`, reports the short URL in its status, and deletes it when the resource is deleted.

```yaml
apiVersion: shortener.example.com/v1alpha1
kind: ShortLink
metadata:
  name: k8s-docs
spec:
  url: https://kubernetes.io/docs
  code: k8s        # optional; defaults to the resource name
```

```text
$ kubectl get shortlinks
NAME       CODE      SHORT URL                               READY   AGE
k8s-docs   k8s       http://shortener.localtest.me/k8s       True    28s
```

This directory is its own Go module (controller-runtime, client-go). `controller-gen` is pinned as a `go tool`.

## Layout

```text
api/v1alpha1/                 ShortLink types and markers; generated deep-copy code
internal/controller/          the reconciler and its tests (fake client)
internal/shortener/           a small client for the shortener API
cmd/manager/                  main: the controller-runtime manager
config/crd/                   generated CRD
config/rbac/                  generated ClusterRole, service account, bindings, leader election
config/manager/               Deployment (2 replicas, leader election)
config/default/               kustomization tying it together
config/samples/               example ShortLinks
```

## Develop

```bash
go mod tidy
go generate ./...            # regenerate deep-copy code, CRD and RBAC after changing markers
go test ./...
go run ./cmd/manager -shortener-url=http://localhost:8080   # against the current kubectl context
```

## Deploy

The shortener must already run in the cluster (see `projects/shortener`, lesson 15.7).

```bash
docker build -t shortlink-operator:dev .     # then load it into your cluster
kubectl apply -k config/default
kubectl -n shortener apply -f config/samples/shortlink.yaml
```

deploy/Dockerfile.content:
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
#
# Build from the repository root:
#   docker build -f deploy/Dockerfile -t gopath-academy:dev .
#   docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 gopath-academy:dev

ARG GO_VERSION=1.24
ARG HUGO_VERSION=0.168.0

# ---------- 1. Build the static site with Hugo ----------
FROM golang:${GO_VERSION}-bookworm AS site
ARG HUGO_VERSION
ARG TARGETARCH
RUN curl -fsSL -o /tmp/hugo.deb \
      "https://github.com/gohugoio/hugo/releases/download/v${HUGO_VERSION}/hugo_extended_${HUGO_VERSION}_linux-${TARGETARCH:-amd64}.deb" \
 && dpkg -i /tmp/hugo.deb \
 && rm /tmp/hugo.deb
WORKDIR /src
# Hugo needs the code folders too: lessons embed files from them.
COPY site/ site/
COPY examples/ examples/
COPY exercises/ exercises/
COPY projects/ projects/
RUN cd site && hugo --minify --gc

# ---------- 2. Build the file server ----------
FROM golang:${GO_VERSION}-bookworm AS server
WORKDIR /src
COPY go.mod ./
COPY deploy/server/ deploy/server/
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w" -o /out/server ./deploy/server

# ---------- 3. Minimal runtime image ----------
FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot
COPY --from=server /out/server /server
COPY --from=site /src/site/public /site
EXPOSE 8080
# A numeric user, so Kubernetes can verify runAsNonRoot (lesson 15.2).
USER 65532:65532
ENTRYPOINT ["/server", "-addr", ":8080", "-dir", "/site"]

deploy/k8s/base/deployment.yaml.content:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: academy
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: academy
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: academy
  strategy:
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 0
      maxSurge: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: academy
    spec:
      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 30
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
        - name: server
          image: gopath-academy
          args: ["-addr", ":8080", "-dir", "/site", "-shutdown-delay", "5s"]
          ports:
            - name: http
              containerPort: 8080
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 5
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: http
            periodSeconds: 10
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 50m
              memory: 32Mi
            limits:
              memory: 64Mi
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities:
              drop: ["ALL"]

        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: academy
                port:
                  name: http

  name: academy

  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: academy
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: http

deploy/k8s/overlays/local/kustomization..content:
# The site on a local cluster (K8s track steps 2 and 3):
#
#   docker build -f deploy/Dockerfile -t gopath-academy:dev .
#   (load the image into the cluster)
#   kubectl apply -k deploy/k8s/overlays/local
#   open http://academy.localtest.me
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: academy
resources:
  - namespace.yaml
  - ../../base
images:
  - name: gopath-academy
    newTag: dev
patches:
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
      name: academy
    patch: |-
      - op: add
        path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/imagePullPolicy
        value: IfNotPresent
